topic: The giant-impact hypothesis and the Moon's origin
title: How was the Moon born? 🌕💥
hook: Did you know the Moon was probably born from a giant crash into Earth?

scenes.narration: Did you know the Moon was probably born from a giant crash into Earth?
About four and a half billion years ago, the Earth was young and covered in lava.
Then another planet, about the size of Mars, came close. Scientists call it Theia.
They collided at an angle, and the impact blasted a huge amount of molten rock into space.
That debris kept circling the Earth, forming a ring.
Bit by bit, gravity pulled the pieces together, and that's how the Moon was born.
At first it was much, much closer and looked huge in the sky, and it has been drifting away ever since.
The evidence: the rocks brought back by the Apollo missions are nearly identical to Earth's.
And the Moon helps us: it keeps Earth's tilt steady, and with it a more stable climate.
Send this to someone who'd give you the Moon.

description: According to the leading hypothesis, about 4.5 billion years ago a Mars-sized planet, Theia, crashed into the young Earth. The debris formed a ring that gravity gathered into the Moon, which started out much closer and has been drifting away. Apollo rocks have a composition nearly identical to Earth's, and the Moon helps stabilize Earth's tilt. Original 3D animation; not to scale.

sources.title: Moon – effect on Earth's axial tilt

claims.statement: The leading hypothesis proposes an impact with a Mars-sized body, called Theia, about 4.5 billion years ago.
Debris from the impact formed a disk around Earth that coalesced into the Moon.
Apollo samples have oxygen isotopes nearly identical to those of Earth rocks.
The Moon helps stabilize the tilt of Earth's axis.
